messages:
nina: Quick doc QA note: noticed inconsistent casing for the request-id header and JSON key across the generate API reference. Some examples use `x-request-id`, others `X-Request-Id`, and response examples flip between `request_id` and `requestId`. This popped up in a customer report.

raph: Can you point to the exact files/lines? I'll triage.

nina: See /docs/reference/generate.md lines ~120-145 and the OpenAPI example in /specs/openapi.yaml. Example curl shows `-H 'x-request-id: trace-1'`. Python and Node snippets vary.

kelly: From runtime side: we normalize incoming headers and surface `requestId` in JSON responses. So canonical header is `X-Request-Id` (we prefer Title-Case) and canonical JSON key is `requestId` (camelCase).

raph: Ok. Proposal: update all examples to Title-Case header `X-Request-Id` and JSON examples to `requestId`. Add a short compatibility note for integrators that older clients may see snake_case and that we accept both in headers.

kelly: Also we should update codegen templates. I found the generator template that maps OpenAPI `request_id` -> Go struct `RequestId` but the YAML uses `request_id` name. If we change OpenAPI example to camelCase we must ensure encoding/field tags still map properly. I'll open a small PR to harmonize the OpenAPI property name with the runtime shape but keep `x-go-field` tags to preserve older generated clients.

nina: Can someone take the docs PR? I'll open an issue with a checklist: update curl/python/go/node snippets, fix OpenAPI example, update migration note, add unit test to docs CI to assert examples match canonical snippets in /specs/examples/request-id.md.

raph: I'll pick it up. Plan: search repo for occurrences of `request_id` and `request-id` and make normalized replacements where examples are concerned. I'll leave actual OpenAPI property rename to @kelly and codegen work to @codegen-bot.

codegen-bot: I updated the template branch to map OpenAPI property `request_id` -> runtime `requestId` using x-field-aliases; pushed diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/codegen/compare/reqid-casing. Generated types will keep JSON tags stable for older clients.

kelly: Reviewed codegen diff. LGTM, small comment about adding a unit in go-generator that validates struct tags include both `json:\"requestId\"` and a `yaml`/`db` tag where appropriate. Not blocking.

raph: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/509. Changes: replace header snippets, update OpenAPI response example to use `requestId`, add migration note in /docs/migration/request-id.md, and add docs-ci test.

docs-ci: Preview build created: https://deploy-preview-509.docs.redwood.ai — tests: docs-lint: passed, links: passed, examples-check: failed (3 mismatched snippets).

nina: Which three?

docs-ci: Mismatches found in: /docs/reference/generate.md (node example), /docs/tutorials/webhook.md (response example), /specs/examples/request-id.md (expected canonical snippet not present). See logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/logs/509-examples.txt

raph: I'll patch those three in the PR now. Also adding a short note in generate.md: "We recommend sending a unique X-Request-Id per client request to aid in tracing."

nina: Thanks. For the migration doc language: keep it minimal: "If you previously parsed `request_id` from responses, update to `requestId`. Header names are case-insensitive; prefer `X-Request-Id` in examples."

kelly: After merge I'll coordinate a codegen release so generated SDKs align. We should include a changelog entry in the release notes about the response key canonicalization.

docs-ci: Examples-check: all matched now. Preview updated: https://deploy-preview-509.docs.redwood.ai (green).

raph: Merged PR 509 at 2945678919.

nina: Awesome. Can we add a short test in examples-check to scan for the lowercase `x-request-id` pattern so it alerts if someone reintroduces the mixed casing?

codegen-bot: Filed a follow-up issue in codegen repo to add the tag validation test.

kelly: Ping me when codegen release is cut; I'll coordinate with eng release calendar.

nina: Thanks folks — closing the loop. If anyone sees a customer still using snake_case, we'll coordinate a migration assist.
